title: What's a Revolution in Military Affairs Good For?
gist: War on the Rocks podcast notes in which Ryan Evans asks Mike Horowitz (Penn), Stacie Pettyjohn (CNAS) and Benjamin Jensen (CSIS) what makes a revolution in military affairs revolutionary, whether one is under way now, and whether it is just drones and AI. The notes pose the questions without stating the panelists' answers.

insights.claim: Militaries have chased the next revolution in warfare for decades, and experts are now debating whether a current revolution in military affairs is under way and whether it extends beyond drones and AI.
insights.speaker: Mike Horowitz, Stacie Pettyjohn, Benjamin Jensen, and Ryan Evans
insights.so_what: Whether drones/AI constitute an RMA shapes long-run defense budget allocation between legacy platforms and autonomy.
insights.quote: Is it just about drones and AI or something more?

insights.claim: The episode examines the promises, pitfalls and persistent myths of military transformation, with Mike Horowitz, Stacie Pettyjohn and Benjamin Jensen.
insights.speaker: Mike Horowitz, Stacie Pettyjohn, Benjamin Jensen, and Ryan Evans
insights.so_what: Skepticism about transformation hype is relevant to valuing defense-tech narratives.
